segments.text: create-spec-driven-app treats specifications as first-class, testable, traceable artifacts. Here is the whole workflow in under two minutes.

Step one: scaffold. A small config file — project name, stack, testing tools — and init generates a complete spec-driven project: a requirements document, a traceability matrix, and a place for Gherkin scenarios.

Step two: apply a domain pack. A pack is versioned, reusable domain knowledge — requirements, use cases, commands, aggregates, events. specops add layers it onto the project the way npm install adds a dependency, and records the source in a lockfile.

Step three: plan. It reads the traceability matrix and the filesystem and tells you, per requirement, exactly what is missing — the feature file, the test, the production code, or just a status update.

Step four: validate. It checks structure, traceability and Gherkin. With the strict T-D-D gate, the build fails whenever the matrix runs ahead of reality — no requirement marked done without its test.

Step five: see the graph. pack lint --graph renders the requirement-to-use-case-to-command-aggregate-event spine as Mermaid, and shouts about any dangling reference — a CI link-check for your domain model.

Step six: automate delivery. The harness runs the plan, context, agent, verify, done loop for every pending requirement, in isolated git worktrees, with any AI agent you configure. Here is a dry run showing the prompt it would hand the agent.
Specs as executable contracts — for humans and AI agents alike. Find it on GitHub and on npm as create-spec-driven-app.
